title: Amped 2
subtitle: A mountain full of possible runs

body: Amped 2 is a freestyle snowboarding game released for Xbox in North America on 28 October 2003. Its mountains offer space to link tricks, explore lines and build a reputation through a career. The player works towards score targets and performs for photographers positioned around each run, making a descent more than a race to the bottom. Developed by Salt Lake Games Studio, the sequel belongs to Microsoft's XSN Sports range. Its focus is the shape and control of a performance: where to take off, what to attempt and how to land.

Completing challenges earns skill points that improve abilities such as spinning, jumping and balance. Progress therefore changes what the rider can attempt, while knowledge of a mountain reveals better places to use those abilities. Media objectives give a particular location a purpose: a trick has to happen where someone can see it. Events offer another route to fame and advancement. The player gradually moves from local rider towards professional recognition, learning to connect the terrain's opportunities with the requirements of an individual challenge instead of treating every jump as interchangeable.

Snow skating adds a smaller board and a different set of possibilities beside conventional snowboarding. The roster includes professional riders such as Jeremy Jones, Torah Bright and Janna Meyen, linking the game to the sport beyond the console. Its licensed soundtrack supports the atmosphere of a filmed riding session, while XSN features connected performance to online competition and rankings. Amped 2 arrived between the original Xbox launch game and Amped 3 on Xbox 360. It develops the earlier game's interest in free riding through more challenges and a broader career.
